versions.changelog: v0.1.2 — version-add workaround republish; content identical to 0.1.1 (minimal-arguments rule + five rules + heuristics/checklist/examples).

v0.1.1 — minimal-arguments rule (working defaults): omit optional tool-call arguments entirely; emit booleans/numbers as bare JSON literals, never quoted. Motivated by a live failure the same day as v0.1.0: an otherwise-atomic call was rejected by a strict tool-call parser because the model emitted a boolean as a string ("background":"false"), crashing the proxy layer. Fewer arguments = fewer type-error surfaces. Since publish, the skill's discipline carried a full operator-driven Airbnb calendar block/unblock round trip on a local model (gpt-oss-120b) — every mutation executed by the agent, zero mega-calls, zero parser deaths.

v0.1.0 — initial release. Atomic tool-call decomposer: five rules (one call = one atomic action; step→observe→step; N steps = N calls; attempted ≠ confirmed; complexity tripwire with payload-to-file defusal), decomposition heuristics + six-point per-call checklist, and a matched good/bad example pair from a real diagnosed production incident (mega-script tool call → parser failure → silent stall). Release evidence: the same local model that stalled on the mega-script completed the harder procedure variant under this skill — 17 atomic calls, zero control-flow offenders, full report.
